title: Define a cheaper companion view linked to a lossless packet

state.decision_rationale: Superseded by MKTCTX/4's explicit review and structure profiles plus signatures, outline, and reference projections. A separate lossy protocol would duplicate those auditable loss semantics.

provenance.source_label: Grok highest-leverage next step: companion view
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Maybe a companion view format that is lossy or summarized for cheaper model context while still pointing back to the lossless packet by hash.
feedback.normalized_claim: Create a derived, budget-conscious view whose omissions and summaries are auditable against an immutable exact packet identity.

current_behavior: Default packets include exact selected UTF-8 source; numbered is the only alternate implemented content view.
Balanced, focused, and structure-only modes are reserved but unimplemented.
Packet and file identities could anchor a separately generated view, but no derived-view relation exists.
evidence: docs/context-format-v3.md: packet identity and exact chunks

proposal.summary: Evaluate a separately identified view artifact that cites a source packet, names its transformation policy, and makes every loss explicit.
candidate_changes: Define source_packet_id and source_manifest_sha256 on every derived view.
Version the view generator, policy, tokenizer, task intent, and budget independently of the lossless packet.
Represent summaries, omitted files, omitted ranges, and exact retained chunks with provenance.
Keep the exact packet retrievable when the view is used for consequential analysis.
Test whether a separate view format is cleaner than adding lossy projections to MKTCTX core.
non_goals: Do not describe summarized content as exact source.
Do not create relevance-based views without explicit intent or policy.
Do not let the derived view silently become the only retained artifact.

questions: Is the companion a MKTCTX profile, a new protocol, or a retrieval plan over an existing packet?
How does a consumer retrieve exact omitted evidence?
What summary provenance and model identity are required?
Can a view remain reusable if it is generated for a specific task?
risks: Lossy views can omit decisive counterevidence.
Model-generated summaries can introduce claims absent from source.
A source packet hash is insufficient if the exact packet is unavailable.
Multiple views add artifact lifecycle and cache complexity.
evidence_needed: Accuracy and cost evaluations against exact packets for review, query, onboarding, and audit tasks.
Provenance and retrieval contract for exact backing content.
Comparison of separate-view and in-protocol projection designs.
